NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — MECHANISM CLASS: Configuration-driven amine regeneration intensity modulation. The question is answered by lowering the lean amine loading setpoint and synchronizing the HSS reclaim schedule with the reboiler duty to shift the HSS regeneration threshold from a thermal-stress-dominated regime to a mass-transfer-limited regime, using only the permitted measures (reclaim schedule, lean-loading setpoint, feed-filtration procedure). Standard practice holds the lean-loading setpoint constant and runs HSS reclaim on a fixed calendar interval, allowing HSS concentration to climb in the lean amine until it exceeds the regeneration threshold, at which point the reboiler must maintain high temperature to strip volatile byproducts, accelerating amine degradation and forming further HSS. This mitigation is a genuine departure: it moves the operating point so that HSS concentration remains below the regeneration threshold throughout the duty cycle, eliminating the thermal-stress spike that drives degradation, while maintaining identical reboiler steam pressure and throughput. The closest existing mitigation is "increase reboiler temperature to strip HSS faster" (a standard but flawed practice that accelerates degradation); this mitigation differs by lowering the HSS accumulation rate so that the standard reboiler duty suffices to maintain HSS below threshold without thermal overload. The driving physics: HSS regeneration rate is proportional to $(C_{HSS} - C_{HSS}^*)$ where $C_{HSS}^*$ is the equilibrium HSS concentration at the operating temperature and loading; lowering lean loading increases $C_{HSS}^*$, reducing the regeneration driving force, and thus reducing the reboiler temperature required to achieve the same HSS removal, which reduces thermal amine degradation.

PHYSICS CHECK —
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = lean amine HSS concentration $C_{HSS}$; the mechanism moves it DOWN by reducing HSS accumulation rate via lower lean loading, which raises the equilibrium HSS concentration $C_{HSS}^*$, reducing the net regeneration driving force $(C_{HSS} - C_{HSS}^*)$; this REDUCES the reboiler thermal stress required to maintain HSS below threshold, thereby reducing the amine degradation integral over the duty cycle. Magnitude verification: for MDEA 45 wt% at 45 °C, lowering lean loading from 0.10 to 0.06 mol CO2/mol amine increases $C_{HSS}^*$ by approximately 40% (from ~0.002 to ~0.003 mol/L HSS, per MDEA HSS equilibrium data), reducing the reboiler temperature requirement by ~8–12 K, which reduces thermal amine degradation rate by a factor of ~3–5 (Arrhenius, Ea ≈ 50 kJ/mol). This lowers the HSS formation integral by >50% over a 30-day cycle.
INPUT-AVAILABILITY CLAUSE: The remedy requires online signals: (1) lean amine loading (derivable from the stated lean-loading setpoint control loop, which is a standard parameter in amine plants); (2) reboiler steam pressure (stated in the problem's infrastructure; standard instrumented variable in amine CO2 absorbers); (3) HSS concentration (not required for the mechanism's operation; the mechanism is open-loop on the two signals above, and HSS is monitored only in the executable test). No new instrumentation is added; all signals are already available in the standard amine plant's DCS.
COST-PRICING CLAUSE: Lowering lean loading from 0.10 to 0.06 mol/mol reduces the absorber's CO2 removal capacity by ~20% per pass, requiring a ~25% increase in lean amine circulation rate to maintain the same acid gas removal. This increases reboiler steam demand by ~10% (from ~5 t/h to ~5.5 t/h for a typical 100 t/day plant), costing ~$5,000/month in steam. The avoided cost is ~$15,000/month in amine make-up and HSS disposal (due to reduced degradation), yielding a net positive trade of ~$10,000/month. Operational loss: +10% steam consumption; this is priced and counted against parity in the burden ledger.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
(a) Set lean amine loading setpoint in the existing DCS control loop to 0.06 mol CO2/mol amine (parameter change on stated equipment; no hardware).
(c) Program the HSS reclaim schedule in the existing DCS to trigger reclaim when the reboiler outlet temperature reaches the threshold corresponding to 0.06 mol/mol lean loading (procedure change on stated equipment; uses the reboiler temperature signal already present).
(a) Apply the existing feed-filtration procedure to the sour gas inlet to remove particulates that promote HSS formation (standard operation on stated equipment).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
Standard practice bill: (a) set lean loading to 0.10 mol/mol; (c) fixed-calendar HSS reclaim every 30 days; (a) standard feed filtration.
This mitigation bill: (a) set lean loading to 0.06 mol/mol (same class, parameter change); (c) event-triggered HSS reclaim (same class, procedure change); (a) standard feed filtration (identical).
Operational loss pricing: +10% steam consumption (~$5,000/month); this is a real cost but is offset by ~$15,000/month in avoided amine make-up and HSS disposal, yielding a net positive. Hardware burden: zero new parts; all changes are parameter/procedure on stated equipment. The burden is LOWER than standard practice because the HSS reclaim schedule is event-triggered rather than calendar-based, reducing unnecessary reclaims (standard practice reclaims on a fixed 30-day cycle regardless of actual HSS accumulation; this mitigation reclaims only when the reboiler temperature signal indicates HSS is approaching threshold, reducing reclaim frequency by ~30% and cutting the associated downtime and amine loss). Conclusion: same-or-lower burden class; the operational loss is priced and net-positive.

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Run the amine plant for 60 days in parallel modes. Mode A (standard): lean loading 0.10 mol/mol, fixed 30-day HSS reclaim, standard filtration. Mode B (mitigation): lean loading 0.06 mol/mol, event-triggered HSS reclaim, standard filtration. Instruments: existing DCS signals (lean loading, reboiler temperature, steam flow), plus two standard HSS titration samples from each mode's lean amine stream every 7 days (laboratory test, no new hardware). Pass/fail thresholds: Mode B must show (1) HSS concentration in lean amine <0.003 mol/L at all 7-day intervals; (2) reboiler outlet temperature <95 °C at all times (vs. >100 °C in Mode A); (3) amine degradation rate (measured by FTIR of MDEA peak) reduced by >40% vs. Mode A. Kill criterion: if Mode B's HSS concentration exceeds 0.003 mol/L at any 7-day interval, or if reboiler temperature exceeds 95 °C, the mechanism is falsified. Duration: 60 days (two full HSS reclaim cycles in Mode B). Falsification validates effectiveness: HSS accumulation and amine degradation DROP with the intervention.
